subject: Contract phasing, start window, and throughput guarantees — Aurora Cloud
messages:
From: Alex Grant <alex.grant@auroracloud.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>; Nicole Park <nicole.park@auroracloud.com>
Cc: procurement@auroracloud.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial sizing + questions on term options

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the performance looked promising. Before we pull procurement in, we need some clarity on a few items so we can map this back to our budget and procurement windows: 

- Can you outline how you recommend we size the GPU pool for our steady-state 150 RPS (p50 1200-token) with occasional spikes to 450 RPS for 10–30 minute windows?
- What do throughput guarantees look like for Dedicated vs dedicated with burst (do you have explicit p99 or per-tenant SLOs we can include in the SOW)?
- On term: we have flexibility for 12 or 24 months; finance pushed back on a 36-month lock. What are the incremental discounts and credits you can offer by term + commit level?

I attached our Q3 usage export for context. Procurement may ask for a start-by date and a phased onramp plan — any standard templates you use?

Appreciate the help,
Alex
Senior Engineering Manager
Aurora Cloud
[Attachment: Aurora_Usage_Report_Q3.csv (csv)]

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Grant <alex.grant@auroracloud.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Initial sizing + questions on term options

Alex — thanks for the detail and the export, that helps a lot. High level answers below, and I'll follow up with a short term/discount matrix + a sample phased onramp we typically include in the SOW.

Sizing recommendation (quick):
- Steady-state 150 RPS (p50 1200-token) maps to ~3 x a100-80GB-equivalent workers for steady throughput with our batching settings; assume 1.8x multiplier for headroom.
- For spikes to 450 RPS, we recommend enabling burst capacity (shared burst pool) sized to handle 2x your historical peak; that typically adds ~2 extra workers.
- If you want hard throughput guarantees (p99), we suggest Dedicated + reserved commit with a 20% safety buffer in the reservation.

SLOs/guarantees:
- Dedicated (baseline): uptime SLA 99.9%, per-request latency SLOs published per model family (we can include p50/p95/p99 buckets in SOW).
- Dedicated + reserved commit & burst: we can commit to a p99 token-time upper bound in the SOW for agreed model/config and traffic profile; this requires an explicit ramp schedule.

Terms/discounts:
- I'll attach a draft matrix (term vs commit) and a sample SOW. Short answer: 12m = standard tier; 24m = ~8–12% effective discount; 36m = ~14–18% (depends on commit size and invoice cadence).

Next steps: I'll put a proposed SOW + phased ramp calendar in your inbox by EOD. Would you prefer a start window of Jan 2027 or Feb 2027? That's when we have capacity openings in us-west for the committed pools.

—Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Draft_SOW_Aurora_v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: Nicole Park <nicole.park@auroracloud.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Grant <alex.grant@auroracloud.com>, procurement@auroracloud.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Initial sizing + questions on term options

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks — Jan would be tight on our end (budget approval cycles), February start looks safer. Two procurement-specific asks:

1) Can you provide a clear table we can drop into our PO that maps committed units -> monthly invoice amount and the effective per-token rate?
2) For ramping, procurement wants an explicit 90-day phased ramp with milestones at 30/60/90 days that tie to credits if Redwood misses throughput targets. Is that something you can include?

I can loop in our procurement lead (procurement@auroracloud.com) if that helps.

Nicole
Director of Product Operations
Aurora Cloud

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Aurora term/credits asks — proposed commit ladder

Jasmine / Neha — forwarding Aurora's asks. Draft proposal below for our outbound:

Proposal (internal):
- Commit tiers: 100 units (base), 250 units, 500 units (units = GPU-equivalent worker-months).
- Term discounts: 12m: baseline price; 24m: 10% recurring credit; 36m: 16% recurring credit.
- Ramp windows: 90-day phased ramp (30/60/90) with 50/80/100% of committed capacity live. If we miss p99 throughput SLA in any milestone window, provide a 10% credit of that window's invoice.
- Burst: allow unpaid burst at up to 20% of committed capacity for first 60 days; beyond that, billed at pay-as-you-go rate unless converted to reserved capacity.

Neha — can you validate the sizing assumptions for the spike handling and confirm ops can guarantee the p99 bounds for the 24m/36m commitments? Also, any recommended language we should avoid in the SOW about hard guarantees?

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 14:33:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Fwd: Aurora term/credits asks — proposed commit ladder

Aditya / Jasmine — validated quickly with infra:
- Sizing looks reasonable given their Q3 export; 3 workers steady + 2 for burst is a safe starting point. Recommend we explicitly mention that guarantees are scoped to the model family, sequence length distribution, and allowed batching parameters.
- Ops comfortable committing to p99 latency bounds for a named model/config under a 24m or 36m reserved commit provided: (a) Aurora agrees to the 90-day ramp milestones and (b) production traffic stays within the profiled distribution.
- Suggest against absolute language like "unlimited burst" or "guaranteed concurrency for any model". Keep it: "guaranteed p99 for agreed config and ramp plan".

I also prepared a short clause for the SOW on credits tied to missed milestone SLOs — I'll paste it into the draft SOW we send.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Grant <alex.grant@auroracloud.com>, Nicole Park <nicole.park@auroracloud.com>, procurement@auroracloud.com
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Final: draft SOW + commit table (Feb start, 90-day ramp)

Alex / Nicole — attaching the updated SOW and a commit table that maps units to monthly invoice amounts. Per your preference we set the start window for Feb 1, 2027 with a 90-day phased ramp (milestones at Feb 1 + Mar 3 + Apr 2). Key points: 

- Term options & effective discounts (examples for 250-unit commit): 12m = baseline; 24m = 10% recurring credit; 36m = 16% recurring credit. Exact numbers in the attached spreadsheet.
- Ramp & credits: 30/60/100% capacity targets at 30/60/90 days; missed p99 throughput for a milestone window triggers a credit equal to 10% of that window's invoice (language in SOW).
- Burst treatment: free burst up to 20% for first 60 days; then pay-as-you-go or convert to reserved capacity.
- SLOs: p50/p95/p99 buckets for the agreed model/config included; p99 is scoped to profiled traffic (language per Neha's note).

Attachments: Draft_SOW_Aurora_v3.pdf, Aurora_Commit_Term_Table.xlsx

Please confirm that Feb 1 start + the milestone credit structure is acceptable and I'll route the SOW to legal and procurement (DocuSign link). Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to review the commit table together.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Aurora_Commit_Term_Table.xlsx (xlsx)]
